html:
Babylonia was the land of southern Mesopotamia, in today's Iraq, named after its chief city, Babylon. On the map it appears from 1500 to 700 BCE.

Babylon first rose under Hammurabi in the 1700s BCE, who united the south and issued his famous law code; this was the Old Babylonian kingdom. After a Hittite raid sacked the city in 1595 BCE, the Kassites, a people from the Zagros mountains, took over and ruled for over four centuries. Kassite Babylon was one of the great powers of its day, writing letters to the pharaohs of Egypt.

After the Kassites fell around 1155 BCE, Babylonia was weaker and often under Assyria, which both honoured and sacked the city. Its scholars kept up cuneiform learning, astronomy and literature, including the Epic of Gilgamesh. In 626 BCE a new dynasty threw off Assyrian rule and built the Neo-Babylonian Empire, which fell to Cyrus of Persia in 539 BCE.
sum: Babylonia was the land of southern Mesopotamia, in today's Iraq, named after its chief city, Babylon. On the map it appears from 1500 to 700 BCE.
